title: Cabling, Switches, and Fiber
summary: Compare copper Ethernet and fiber paths while practicing safe labeling and cable management.
objectives: Compare copper Ethernet and fiber roles at a high level.
Use labels and a diagram to document a physical network path.

vocab.def: A fiber type designed for light traveling in one main path over long distances.
A fiber type designed for light traveling in multiple paths over shorter distances.
Organizing and labeling cables so paths are clear and maintainable.

sections.heading: Different links fit different needs
sections.body: Copper Ethernet and fiber both carry network information. Fiber uses light and is useful for high-capacity or longer links. Single-mode and multimode describe fiber designs at a conceptual level.

sections.heading: Physical organization is technical work
sections.body: Labels, routes, ports, and documentation help people understand a network. A clear path supports troubleshooting and reduces accidental disconnection.

sections.heading: Safe cabling lab
sections.body: Use classroom patch cables, yarn, or paper links. Never inspect live fiber, handle glass fragments, use lasers, or operate professional termination tools without qualified training.

practice.prompt: Document a path from a server to a switch and then to a gateway. Choose copper or fiber for one link and explain your conceptual reason.

quiz.question: Why is cable management useful?
options: It makes physical paths clearer and easier to maintain
It eliminates the need for switches
quiz.answer: It makes physical paths clearer and easier to maintain

lab.objective: Build and label a non-live classroom network path model.
